Available in this preview

RAM, CPUs, lifetime and keep-alive are configurable. Disk management supports offline expansion/shrink, compaction and a retained recovery disk. Stock networking uses a proxy and explicit UDP/ping; the custom kernel optionally adds ordinary TCP/UDP/DNS. Direct USB, GPU Vulkan and hardware video remain unavailable.
Host protection

Android’s kernel, boot partitions and SELinux stay unchanged; no Android reboot. Choose stock Microdroid or a verified guest image in private app storage. Root and Gunyah are required. This route has no pvmfw verified boot or equivalent AVF guarantee.
Setup

1. Use the buttons above to enable Terminal and open its Linux installer.
2. In Vector, enable this module for Terminal only.
3. Allow root here, then open Terminal.

Network behavior

Network egress uses the selected Android app UID and its INTERNET permission, VPN and power policy. Terminal is the default; the experimental profile can explicitly choose Bridge for its fullscreen GUI. Background/Doze restrictions can block either app. No host routes, DNS, firewall or power restrictions are changed.
OpenGL acceleration

Run plb-install-gpu inside Linux, then save graphics settings here and recreate only the VM. Android restart is unnecessary. virgl (Adreno) in plb-gpu-info indicates host GPU OpenGL. Weston composition and direct Android GPU viewing have separate switches. Capture and copying still use CPU. Zero-copy and GPU Vulkan are not supported.
Network tools

ping -c 4 1.1.1.1 sends real IPv4 echo requests without raw sockets. plb-udp-forward 5353 1.1.1.1 53 forwards guest localhost:5353 to the specified UDP destination until interrupted. Configure your tool to use that local port. This is explicit forwarding, not transparent networking. Host-local, link-local and multicast destinations are blocked.

Choose stock Microdroid or experimental Linux 6.18.57-plb1. Experimental use copies Debian into a separate disk, initially 512 MiB / 1 CPU / CPU graphics. Gunyah memory allocation can terminate the VM under heavier workloads. Android’s kernel and boot partitions stay unchanged; host-failure risk is not zero.

Experimental network

TCP, UDP and DNS without per-app proxy settings, using a TUN interface inside the custom-kernel VM. Android routing and firewall stay unchanged. DNS uses 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8; traffic follows the selected Android app’s network/VPN policy. Background restrictions on that app may block it; choose Bridge for its GUI. No incoming ports, broadcast or arbitrary IP protocols. Ping uses the existing plb-ping relay.

Save Linux work first. This stops only this VM. Resize and compaction create and verify offline copies. The previous disk is retained. Restoring swaps the two disks, retaining both. Android will not reboot.
Delete the previous recovery disk permanently? The current disk is retained. This cannot be undone.

Applies to the selected Debian profile. Thin qcow2 grows with use. Virtual capacity, Android allocation and Linux usage are different. Shrink requires enough room for data and filesystem metadata. Copies need additional temporary space. Free-space recovery zeroes unused blocks on a copy; the current disk is never truncated. A retained previous disk must be restored or explicitly deleted before another resize/compaction.

Android 17 guest · experimental

Run a separate Android 17 VM with 1.5 GiB or the original 512 MiB. Two CPUs, 480 × 800, software rendering. The older 1.5 GiB runtime reached home, but its refault method was retired after a host page-cache warning. The current prefault-only runtime is not boot-validated and refuses known host page errors. Prepared OS images are required.

The 1.5 GiB mode refuses startup if host page-management failures are recorded. The 1.5 GiB mode temporarily uses up to 6 GiB of RAM during preparation. Background apps may be reclaimed. Startup changes the host-wide 16/32/64 KiB shmem THP settings to advise for about 10 seconds, then restores them. An independent guardian attempts restoration at its 40-second deadline on failure.\n\nOn first use, the existing Android disks are copied. Later data is stored separately from the 512 MiB profile. Debian is stopped and its disks are preserved. Closing this viewer stops only this VM. Maximum session: 30 minutes. Guest networking, audio, physical USB and hardware graphics are not supported.
